summary: Deployed PostgreSQL 9.5 branch_stock on node1 with the supplied records intact. stock_app on node2 can read stock and update only quantity; it cannot read supplier_costs or modify schema. auditor can read both tables but cannot write. Separate credentials persist with mode 0600. Both nodes were rebooted sequentially and fully recovered with changed boot IDs.
actions_performed: Installed Ubuntu 16.04-compatible PostgreSQL 9.5 packages without changing the OS release or kernel
Imported the supplied stock.sql into branch_stock on node1
Created restricted stock_app and auditor database roles
Created separate node2 service accounts and credential files
Restricted remote role access to node2
Tested permitted and denied operations directly
Restarted node1 and node2 one at a time and verified persistence

evidence.requirement: branch_stock schema and supplied records deployed on node1
evidence.summary: Schema import succeeded; PAPER=40, LABELS=18 and supplier costs 3.25/1.75 remain present.

evidence.requirement: stock_app can read stock and update quantities, but cannot change schema or read supplier_costs
evidence.summary: Direct tests demonstrated stock reads and a transactional quantity update, while supplier access, schema creation, and SKU updates were denied before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: auditor has read-only access to stock and supplier_costs
evidence.summary: Auditor read both tables successfully; update attempts were denied.
Credentials are distinct, stored separately, owned by their node2 service accounts, and mode 0600; both remained functional after reboot.
Both source copies retained SHA-256 7934fb042f67368428ae2fcf771fef48d1e6154f8d0d1e6b1c9d144c7d5622ea, and final database values match the supplied SQL.

evidence.requirement: Legacy operating system and kernel retained
evidence.summary: Both nodes remained Ubuntu 16.04.7 LTS with kernel 4.4.0-210-generic; PostgreSQL 9.5.25 came from the compatible distribution repository.

Baseline boot ID 4b7ded33-b5e2-42c9-b7f2-bd671942a82d, restart acknowledgement, changed ID 6c228068-b177-48b6-a035-ebe388363ff5, active PostgreSQL, intact data/privileges, and successful remote role access were proven.

Baseline boot ID 0256e3f5-9f2d-48f3-b55b-12f9f4d599ab, restart acknowledgement, changed ID 563df753-7eca-4f22-9518-bfee4f9d7556, restored credentials/client access, and final node1 database health were proven.
